newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian RAMS team sets up new bank.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian RAMS team sets up new bank.

text.p: A new investment bank specialising in securitisation, Australian Securitised Funding, has been establised by the team responsible for organising funding for non-bank lender RAMS Home Loans.
ASF chief executive Robin Redfern said the company would begin operations with an agreement to finance the residential mortgages of RAMS.
The bank will also be backed by several large international shareholders to be announced in the next two months.

ASF's creation is a first in Australia and is expected to provide a major source of finance for the burgeoning non-bank home loan market, as well as other businesses such as small and medium-sized enterprises.

Redfern said that while ASF's creation stemmed from RAMS' success in innovative securitisation, the home loan company was now "merely a client" and would operate on the same terms as all other ASF clients.
Mortgages on RAMS books now total more than A$1.0 billion, with the company predicting a further A$1.0 billion a year in business.
"We'll be using our finance and structuring knowledge to assist other mortgage orignators and companies to find effective offbalance sheet asset backed funding," Redfern said.
In additional to residential mortgages, ASF expects to finance assets such as commercial mortgages, small and medium enterprise loans, personal loans, trade receivables, property and leases.
"The securitisation market is still opening up and it's possible that other assets, such as royalities, might become securitised as the market grows," Redfern said.

He added that he anticipated that most assets would need to be pooled or credit enhanced in order to be securitised, although large assets and/or assets of a very secure nature may require less structuring.

Redfern said he expected ASF's services would be highly sought after as it had the expertise not only to structure suitable funding but also manage bond programmes, maintain accounts and registers, and ensure proper compliance.
"While securitisation is becoming a more common form of funding it is still a relatively new. ASF can offer experience in the area as well as innovative ideas on new ways to raise funds."

Redfern was responsible for trading Australian and Canadian mortage backed securities at brokerage firm Ord Minnett prior to joining RAMS, and created ANZ McCaughan's securitised bond programme which funded more than A$1.0 billion in assets.
He also established the initial securitisation programme for PUMA, while at Schroders.
